summary.text: Jordan Wright has represented Assembly District 70 in Central Harlem since January 2025. A graduate of Syracuse University, he worked as an educator in Manhattan schools, served on his local community board, and was chief of staff to City Council Member Yusef Salaam. He is the son of former Assembly Member Keith L.T. Wright, won the open seat in 2024, and defeated Conrad Blackburn in the June 2026 Democratic primary; he is the only candidate listed for the November general election.

paragraphs.text: Wright is a lifelong New Yorker and a resident of Central Harlem; Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as New York, New York.
He graduated from Syracuse University in 2017 with a degree in psychology.

After college he worked as an educator in multiple Manhattan schools, and he served for a number of years on his local community board, which according to his official biography coincided with the Covid-19 pandemic.

He was Chief of Staff to New York City Council Member Yusef Salaam, and according to NY1 had earlier been Salaam's campaign manager; he resigned the chief of staff post to take his Assembly seat in January 2025.

In June 2024 he won a four-way Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 70 seat, receiving over 48% of the vote according to NY1; then-Assembly Member Inez Dickens, the seat's incumbent, backed him. He was elected in November 2024 and took office in January 2025.

In the 2025-2026 session he serves on the Aging, Banks, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Libraries and Education Technology, Racing and Wagering, and Transportation committees.
On June 23, 2026 he defeated Conrad Blackburn in the Democratic primary, 53.9% to 45.7%.

He is the son of former Assembly Member Keith L.T. Wright and the grandson of former New York Supreme Court Judge Bruce Wright, and, according to his official biography, is a member of St. Phillip's Episcopal Church.
